'''Peter Murray-Rust''' is a chemist currently working at the [[University of Cambridge]]. As well as his work in chemistry, Murray-Rust is also known for his support of [[open access]] and [[open data]].

==Education==
He was educated at [[Bootham School]],{{Citation needed|date=April 2023}} a [[Private schools in the United Kingdom|private school]] in [[York]], and at [[Balliol College, Oxford]]. After obtaining a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] with a thesis entitled ''A structural investigation of some compounds showing charge-transfer properties'', he became lecturer in chemistry at the (new) [[University of Stirling]] and was first warden of Andrew Stewart Hall of Residence. In 1982, he moved to [[GlaxoSmithKline|Glaxo]] Group Research at Greenford to head Molecular Graphics,<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Murray-Rust | first1 = P. | author-link1 = Peter Murray-Rust| last2 = Glusker | first2 = J. P. | doi = 10.1021/ja00316a034 | title = Directional hydrogen bonding to sp2- and sp3-hybridized oxygen atoms and its relevance to ligand-macromolecule interactions | journal = Journal of the American Chemical Society | volume = 106 | issue = 4 | pages = 1018–1025 | year = 1984 }}</ref> Computational Chemistry and later protein structure determination. He was Professor of [[Pharmacy]] in the [[University of Nottingham]] from 1996 to 2000, setting up the Virtual School of Molecular Sciences. He is now [[Reader (academic rank)|Reader]] [[Emeritus]] in Molecular Informatics at the [[University of Cambridge]] and Senior Research Fellow Emeritus at [[Churchill College, Cambridge]].

==Research==
His research interests have involved the automated analysis of data in scientific publications, creation of virtual communities, e.g. The Virtual School of Natural Sciences in the Globewide Network Academy, and the [[Semantic Web]]. With [[Henry Rzepa]], he has extended this to chemistry through the development of [[markup language]]s, especially [[Chemical Markup Language]].<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Murray-Rust | first1 = P. | author-link1 = Peter Murray-Rust| last2 = Rzepa | first2 = H. S. | author-link2 = Henry Rzepa| doi = 10.1021/ci990052b | title = Chemical Markup, XML, and the Worldwide Web. 1. Basic Principles | journal = Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling | volume = 39 | issue = 6 | pages = 928–942 | year = 1999 }}</ref> He campaigns for [[open data]], particularly in science, and is on the advisory board of the [[Open Knowledge International]] and a co-author of the [[Panton Principles]] for Open scientific data.<ref>http://pantonprinciples.org/ {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170622184818/https://pantonprinciples.org/ |date=22 June 2017 }} Panton Principles for Open data in science</ref> Together with a few other chemists, he was a founder member of the [[Blue Obelisk]] movement in 2005.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Guha | first1 = R. | last2 = Howard | first2 = M. In 2002, Peter Murray-Rust and his colleagues proposed an electronic repository for unpublished chemical data called the [[World Wide Molecular Matrix]] (WWMM). In January 2011, a symposium around his career and visions was organized, called ''Visions of a Semantic Molecular Future''.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Jones | first1 = R. | last2 = MacGillivray | first2 = M. | last3 = Murray-Rust | first3 = P. | author-link3 = Peter Murray-Rust| last4 = Pitman | first4 = J. | last5 = Sefton | first5 = P. | last6 = O'Steen | first6 = B. | last7 = Waites | first7 = W. | title = Open Bibliography for Science, Technology, and Medicine | doi = 10.1186/1758-2946-3-47 | journal = Journal of Cheminformatics | volume = 3 | pages = 47 | year = 2011 | pmid =  21999661| pmc =3206455 | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>CCL Archives, 2010, http://ccl.net/chemistry/resources/messages/2010/11/12.005-dir/</ref><ref>Meeting Archives and publications, 2011, http://www.dspace.cam.ac.uk/handle/1810/238409</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Murray-Rust | first1 = P. | author-link1 = Peter Murray-Rust| doi = 10.1186/1758-2946-3-48 | title = Semantic science and its communication - a personal view | journal = Journal of Cheminformatics | volume = 3 | page = 48| year = 2011 | pmid =  21999715| pmc =3206456 | doi-access = free }}</ref> In 2011, he and Henry Rzepa were joint recipients of the [[Herman Skolnik Award]] of the [[American Chemical Society]].<ref>CCL Archives, 2011, http://www.ccl.net/cgi-bin/ccl/message-new?2011+09+26+014</ref> In 2014, he was awarded a Fellowship by the [[Shuttleworth Foundation]] to develop the automated mining of science from the literature.

In 2009 Murray-Rust coined the term ''"Doctor Who" model'' for the phenomenon exhibited by the [[Blue Obelisk]] project and other Open Science projects, where when a project leader does not have the resources to continue to lead a project (e.g. because he or she has moved to another university with other tasks), someone else will stand up to become the new leader and continue the project.<ref>Glyn Moody, The Doctor Who Model of Open Source, 2009, http://opendotdotdot.blogspot.nl/2009/06/doctor-who-model-of-open-source.html</ref><ref>P. Murray-Rust, The Doctor Who Model of Open Source, 2009, http://blogs.ch.cam.ac.uk/pmr/2009/06/06/the-doctor-who-model-of-open-source/</ref> This is a reference to the long-running British science fiction television series ''[[Doctor Who]]'', in which the main character periodically [[Regeneration (Doctor Who)|regenerates]] into a different form, which is played by a different actor.

As of 2014, Murray-Rust was granted a Fellowship by [[Shuttleworth Foundation]] in relation to the ContentMine project which uses machines to liberate 100,000,000 facts from the scientific literature.<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20140731042233/http://contentmine.org/ Article title]}}</ref>

In recent years, Murray-Rust has been active in the #semanticClimate project, which focuses on semantifying climate data, IPPC reports, and generally making climate knowledge open and machine readable and actionable.<ref>{{cite web |title=Climate AI outreach in India {{!}} Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry |url=https://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/news/climate-ai-outreach-india |website=ch.cam.ac.uk |access-date=21 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite Q|Q137043396}}</ref>

==Activism==
Murray-Rust is also known for his work on making scientific knowledge from literature freely available, and in such taking a stance against publishers that are not fully compliant with the [[Berlin Declaration on Open Access to Knowledge in the Sciences and Humanities|Berlin Declaration on Open Access]]. In 2014, he actively raised awareness of glitches in the publishing system of [[Elsevier]], where restrictions were imposed by Elsevier on the reuse of papers after the authors had paid Elsevier to make the paper freely available.<ref>Paul Jump, Elsevier: bumps on road to open access, Times Higher Education, 2014, http://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/news/elsevier-bumps-on-road-to-open-access/2012238.article</ref>
